key_changes_vs_previous: Wheelbase +57 mm (2,211 → 2,268 mm): the rear wheels moved back on longer semi-trailing arms without lengthening the body, to calm the tail-happy handling; the front ballast weights were deleted.
Wheel openings reworked/slightly flared for wider wheels (5½J on the T, 6J on the E/S); the battery was split into two units, one in each front wing area, for better weight balance.
Mechanical fuel injection for the new 911 E and the 911 S; die-cast magnesium engine parts saved 16 kg; the 911 T kept carburettors.
Targa gained a fixed, heated glass rear window as standard (MY1969); sealed body cavities were added against rust (1969), and hot-dip zinc underbody protection followed for MY1971.

Displacement grew to 2.2 litres (MY1970) and 2.4 litres (MY1972, with the Type 915 gearbox). The MY1970 C-series got door handles with a concealed lever; the 2.4-litre cars got a black engine-lid grille with a '2.4' badge and black anodised lettering, MY1972 had a one-year-only oil-filler flap, and MY1973 added black horn grilles and rectangular mirrors.

Engines grew to 2.2 litres (1970) and 2.4 litres (1972): the entry 911 T went from 110 to 130 PS while the 911 S reached 190 PS and 230 km/h.
03-911-lwb-1969.fun_fact: For model year 1972 only, the oil tank sat ahead of the right rear wheel behind its own filler flap — dropped after one year, reportedly because fuel attendants kept pouring petrol into it.

key_changes_vs_previous: About 85% of the parts newly developed (Porsche), while keeping the G-model silhouette.
Front and rear panels of deformable plastic, with number plate, air intakes, indicators and fog lights integrated into the front bumper for the first time; new sill covers and optimised rain gutters.
Electric rear spoiler that rises automatically above 80 km/h replaces the fixed/optional spoiler; smooth underbody. Cd fell to 0.32, the most aerodynamic air-cooled 911.
New 3.6-litre M64 flat-six (+400 cc) with twin-spark ignition, knock control and three-way catalyst: 250 PS versus 231 PS for the Carrera 3.2.
MacPherson struts and coil springs at the front, coil springs on semi-trailing arms at the rear replace the torsion bars used since 1963.
ABS and power steering standard; driver and passenger airbags standard from 1991; Tiptronic automatic from 1990; all-wheel drive (Carrera 4) for the first time.
Fuchs wheels give way to 16-inch Design 90 wheels; fuel tank reduced from 85 to 77 litres.
09-964-1989.summary: The 964 kept the classic 911 silhouette, but about 85% of it was new: a 250 PS 3.6-litre twin-spark flat-six, coil-spring suspension, ABS and power steering, and on the Carrera 4 the first all-wheel-drive 911. 09-964-1989.fun_fact: The 964's rear spoiler rises by itself at about 80 km/h to cut lift and push more cooling air to the engine, and Porsche patented the design.

key_changes_vs_previous: Porsche: practically only the roofline was carried over from the 964; about 400 million DM and four years of development.
Flatter, wider front wings with poly-ellipsoid headlights replace the upright 'tunnel' headlamps; a shorter front lid removes the black rubber lip between the body and the front bumper.
More fully integrated bumpers with side lights, fog lights and indicators; interplay of concave and convex surfaces; teardrop-shaped mirrors.
Wider rear wings running in straighter lines; a full-width angled light strip with integrated tail lights set higher; a larger automatically extending rear spoiler.
New aluminium LSA multi-link rear axle, the final step of the 'Weissach axle' idea, replaces the semi-trailing arms; rear track widened from 1,374 to about 1,445 mm.
The first 6-speed manual in a 911 (5-speed before); Tiptronic S with steering-wheel switches from MY1995.

Engine uprated to 272 PS (from 250) with hydraulic valve lifters, a stiffer crankshaft, lighter rods and pistons and a dual-flow exhaust with two catalysts; longer service intervals; VarioRam 285 PS from MY1996.
Luggage space up 20% to 123 litres; larger cross-drilled brakes; coupé kerb weight up only about 20 kg on the 964.

Porsche kept little more than the 964's roof, adding flatter wings with ellipsoid headlights, wider hips, a multi-link rear axle and the 911's first six-speed gearbox. Its 3.6-litre flat-six made 272 PS, and 285 PS from the 1996 model year.
10-993-1994.fun_fact: The last air-cooled 911, a Carrera 4S ordered by Jerry Seinfeld, was completed on 31 March 1998, four days after Ferry Porsche died.

key_changes_vs_previous: T-Hybrid performance hybrid in the GTS (3.6-litre, electric turbocharger, e-motor in PDK) — the first hybrid road 911.
Carrera engine revised: turbochargers from the old GTS and intercooler from the Turbo, +9 PS to 394 PS.
Matrix LED headlights standard with every light function built in, so the front driving lights disappear and the cooling intakes grow; each model gets its own bumper.
Rear: redesigned light strip with an integrated arc and 'PORSCHE' lettering, a five-fin rear grille per side, higher number plate, exhausts set into the diffuser fins; length +23 mm to 4,542 mm.
First fully digital 911 instrument cluster (12.6-inch curved), start button replaces the key (still left of the wheel); coupé 2-seater as standard (2+2 at no cost).
Larger brakes on the Carrera (350 mm discs, six-piston front calipers); launch Carreras PDK-only.
18-992-2-2024.summary: The 992.2 facelift brought the first hybrid 911: the GTS T-Hybrid, with an electric turbocharger and 541 PS. The base Carrera got 394 PS, matrix LED headlights with every light built in, a new light bar and the 911's first fully digital instruments.
18-992-2-2024.fun_fact: The 992.2 is the first 911 with a push-button start, and Porsche still put the button to the left of the steering wheel, as the ignition key always was.
